Do NOT git commit, branch, or push; leave changes uncommitted. No skills/MCP/network. PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1. These findings come from a composition review of the just-landed Phase 3 (commits 13af541..e51f0ee) - line refs are current. Fail closed; no silent substitution; no duplicate provider effects.

OWNERSHIP: you own ONLY: server/pipeline/orchestrator.py, server/pipeline/ledger.py, server/pipeline/social.py, tests/test_orchestrator.py, tests/test_publish_orchestrator_resume_fanout.py, tests/test_social.py, tests/test_zernio.py, tests/test_publishing.py. Never modify anything else.

FINDINGS (each: fix + proving test):
1. HIGH ledger.py:212 - the per-episode fanout budget is consumed BEFORE the idempotency claim and never released, so failed attempts/concurrent losers exhaust the budget without completing actions. Fix: consume only after the idempotency claim succeeds (or reserve-then-release on failure with a crash-safe release marker); a replayed already-created action must not consume budget twice.
2. HIGH orchestrator.py:368 - missing/malformed approved_clips normalizes to [], so corruption reads as legally-empty and publishes without Short coverage. Fix: distinguish three states - explicit [] (legal, proceed), key absent on an episode that produced clips (halt to review: manifest expected), unparseable/malformed (halt to review). An episode whose pipeline produced zero clips may carry explicit [].
3. HIGH orchestrator.py:3856 - social retries regenerate schedule identities from mutable content/calendar state, so changed text/order/dates mint new receipt keys and duplicate posts. Fix: persist the per-post identity list (keys + schedules + text-hashes) ONCE at first materialization in episode.json; every retry consumes the stored identities and only fills missing/failed ones; content changes after materialization require an explicit re-materialization that first reconciles against provider receipts.
4. HIGH orchestrator.py:797 - promo assets are inferred from the polished manifest/clip dir despite explicit approved_clips. Fix: _promo_asset_plan sources ONLY approved_clips; explicit [] plans no clip uploads (episode artwork/social image still allowed per its own list); stale/rejected clips never upload.
5. HIGH orchestrator.py:922 - social binding strips authored media before verification, and Twitter is excluded from required-media validation, silently scheduling text-only. Fix: verification check runs BEFORE any stripping; a post authored WITH media whose URL is unverified = per-post failure (never text-only fallback), uniformly across platforms; a post authored text-only stays legal. Any intentional platform-specific media rule must be an explicit named constant with a comment, not an exclusion in the check.
6. HIGH social.py:30 - apply_social_blackout has NO production caller. Fix: wire it into the production scheduling path (where posts are finalized before per-post dispatch) with reserved_dates derived from the publish calendar's launch dates; back-catalog campaigns shift, launch campaigns never do; add the call-site test.

TESTS: budget-not-consumed-on-failed-claim + released-on-failure + replay-no-double-consume (ledger); corrupted-manifest halts vs explicit-empty proceeds; retry-uses-stored-identities (mutate text between attempts, assert no new key and no duplicate dispatch); promo plan ignores unapproved clips; authored-media-unverified fails per-post on every platform incl. twitter; blackout invoked in the real path (dispatch-capture proves shifted back-catalog + unshifted launch). ALL existing tests green (list contract updates).

HOW TO RUN: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_orchestrator.py tests/test_publish_orchestrator_resume_fanout.py tests/test_social.py tests/test_zernio.py tests/test_publishing.py -q -p no:cacheprovider
